name: Wall Drug
remarks: Legendary roadside stop famous for hundreds of highway billboards and free ice water since 1936.

name: Corn Palace
remarks: Unique arena decorated annually with murals made entirely from corn and grain, rebuilt each year with new themes.

name: Dinosaur Park
remarks: Seven life-sized concrete dinosaur sculptures built in 1936 overlooking the city from a hilltop park.

name: Cadillac Ranch
remarks: Ten Cadillacs half-buried nose-first in the Texas Panhandle, a public art installation created in 1974 by the Ant Farm collective.

name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
remarks: Famous Route 66 steakhouse offering a free 72-oz steak challenge if eaten in under one hour.

name: Leaning Tower of Texas
remarks: A deliberately tilted water tower built as a marketing gimmick by Ralph Britten to lure drivers off I-40 into his truck stop.

name: Conoco Tower Station and U-Drop Inn
remarks: A stunning 1936 Art Deco roadside masterpiece on Route 66, now a welcome center listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

name: Devil's Rope Museum
remarks: A Route 66 museum housing the world's largest collection of barbed wire and publications about its history.

name: Stonehenge II and Easter Island Heads
remarks: A 90%-scale Stonehenge replica accompanied by two Easter Island moai replicas, built by Al Shepperd in a Texas Hill Country field.

name: Cabazon Dinosaurs
remarks: Iconic giant concrete dinosaurs — Mr. Rex and Dinny — visible from I-10, featured in Pee-wee's Big Adventure.

name: Madonna Inn
remarks: Eccentric hotel with 110 uniquely themed rooms, a famous waterfall urinal in the men's room, and pink everywhere.
address: 100 Madonna Rd, San Luis Obispo, CA 93405

name: Salvation Mountain
remarks: Colorful folk art installation in the Sonoran Desert created by Leonard Knight over two decades using adobe and paint.

name: Mystery Spot
remarks: A gravity-defying tourist attraction in the redwoods where balls roll uphill and people stand at impossible angles.
address: 465 Mystery Spot Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95065

name: Winchester Mystery House
remarks: A Victorian mansion with 160 rooms, staircases to nowhere, and doors opening into walls, built continuously for 38 years by Sarah Winchester.
address: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128

name: Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch
remarks: A surreal forest of welded metal trees adorned with thousands of colorful glass bottles along Route 66, created by Elmer Long.
address: 24266 National Trails Hwy, Oro Grande, CA 92368

name: Bigfoot Discovery Museum
remarks: A small museum in the Santa Cruz Mountains with footprint casts, the Patterson-Gimlin film, and a 9-foot Bigfoot statue out front.

name: Glass Beach
remarks: A former dump site turned tourist gem where decades of ocean tumbling transformed broken glass into smooth colorful sea glass pebbles.
address: Glass Beach Dr, Fort Bragg, CA 95437

name: Roy's Motel and Cafe
remarks: A restored Googie-architecture gas station and motel in a Mojave ghost town, an iconic Route 66 relic.

name: Integratron
remarks: A non-metallic all-wood dome built by UFO contactee George Van Tassel in the Mojave Desert, used today for sound bath healing sessions.

name: Carhenge
remarks: A replica of England's Stonehenge built from 38 vintage American automobiles spray-painted gray, on the Nebraska plains.

name: Boys Town
remarks: The famous village for troubled youth founded by Father Flanagan in 1917, known for the iconic statue of a boy carrying another with the motto 'He ain't heavy.'

name: The Blue Whale of Catoosa
remarks: A smiling 80-foot blue whale sculpture built in the 1970s beside a pond on historic Route 66.

name: Golden Driller
remarks: A 76-foot, 43,500-pound statue of a shirtless oil worker, the fifth-tallest free-standing statue in the United States.

name: Pops 66 Soda Ranch
remarks: A Route 66 restaurant and soda shop with over 700 varieties of soda and a massive glowing soda bottle sculpture out front.

name: Arcadia Round Barn
remarks: A rare 1898 round barn on Route 66 restored by volunteers in 1992, now housing a local history museum and gift shop.

name: London Bridge
remarks: The original London Bridge purchased from the City of London in 1968 and rebuilt stone by stone in the Arizona desert.
address: 1340 McCulloch Blvd N, Lake Havasu City, AZ 86403

name: Biosphere 2
remarks: A 3.14-acre enclosed research facility that housed eight scientists in a sealed ecological experiment from 1991 to 1993.

name: Standin' on the Corner Park
remarks: A small Route 66 park commemorating the Eagles lyric about standing on a corner in Winslow, Arizona.

name: The Thing
remarks: A mid-century sideshow attraction teased for miles by billboards on I-10, featuring alleged mummies, aliens, and Cold War curiosities.

name: Wigwam Motel No. 6
remarks: One of three surviving Wigwam Village motels in the US, with air-conditioned concrete teepee-shaped rooms on Route 66 since the 1950s.

name: Jolly Green Giant Statue
remarks: A 55-foot fiberglass statue of the Jolly Green Giant, accompanied by a museum celebrating the canned vegetable mascot.

name: SPAM Museum
remarks: A free museum dedicated entirely to SPAM canned meat, created by Hormel Foods in the product's hometown.

name: World's Largest Ball of Twine
remarks: A 12-foot, 17,400-pound ball of twine wound entirely by one man, Francis A. Johnson, over 29 years.

name: World's Largest Ball of Twine by Community
remarks: A community-grown ball of twine started in 1953 by Frank Stoeber, now weighing over 26,000 lbs — the largest by weight.

name: Cars on the Route (Kan-O-Tex Service Station)
remarks: A restored 1934 gas station on Route 66 said to have inspired Tow Mater from Pixar's Cars, featuring a grinning tow truck out front.

name: World's Largest Easel
remarks: An 80-foot steel easel on the Kansas plains displaying a giant reproduction of Van Gogh's Three Sunflowers, visible from I-70.

name: World's Smallest Church
remarks: A tiny one-room church seating exactly one person, built in 1934 and still standing as a roadside curiosity on the Kansas plains.

name: Jimmy Carter Peanut Statue
remarks: A towering smiling peanut statue built to celebrate Jimmy Carter's 1976 presidential campaign in his hometown.

name: World's Largest Peanut
remarks: A giant peanut on a pedestal celebrating Georgia's status as a leading peanut-producing state.

name: World of Coca-Cola
remarks: A museum dedicated to the world's most famous soft drink, with secret vault, memorabilia, and a global soda tasting room.

name: Leaning Tower of Niles
remarks: A half-scale replica of Italy's Leaning Tower of Pisa built in 1934 by Robert Ilg as a water tank for a nearby pool.

name: World's Largest Catsup Bottle
remarks: A 170-foot water tower shaped like a bottle of Brooks Catsup, built in 1949 and now a beloved Route 66 icon.

name: Superman Statue
remarks: A 15-foot bronze statue of Superman in the town that officially adopted the name of his fictional home city.

name: Gemini Giant (Muffler Man)
remarks: A 30-foot fiberglass Muffler Man spaceman holding a rocket, named after NASA's Gemini program, on Route 66 since the 1960s.

name: Paul Bunyon Hot Dog Muffler Man
remarks: A 19-foot fiberglass giant brandishing an oversized hot dog, saved by locals after his advertising restaurant closed in 2002.

name: Railsplitter Covered Wagon
remarks: The world's largest covered wagon at 24 feet tall, featuring a statue of Abraham Lincoln perched on top along Route 66.

name: Henry's Rabbit Ranch
remarks: A Route 66 stop mixing live bunnies with retired Volkswagen Rabbits in an elaborate pun-filled roadside display.

name: Fremont Troll
remarks: An 18-foot concrete sculpture of a troll clutching a real VW Beetle beneath the Aurora Bridge, built by artists in 1990.
address: N 36th St & Troll Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103

name: Grandfather Cuts Loose the Ponies
remarks: Fifteen life-sized steel horse silhouettes galloping across a basalt ridge overlooking the Columbia River, installed in 1989.
address: Wild Horse Monument Rd, Vantage, WA 98950

name: Benewah Milk Bottle Building
remarks: A giant milk bottle-shaped building that has been a Spokane landmark since 1935, now home to Dry Fly Distilling.

name: Enchanted Forest
remarks: A hand-built fantasy theme park carved out of wilderness starting in 1964 by Roger Tofte, still family-owned and operated.

name: Oregon Vortex
remarks: A classic mystery spot where brooms stand on their own, people appear to change height, and balls roll uphill in a former assay office.
address: 4303 Sardine Creek L Fork Rd, Gold Hill, OR 97525

name: Ave Maria Grotto
remarks: A 4-acre park with 125 miniature reproductions of famous religious sites built by Benedictine monk Brother Joseph Zoettl.
address: 1600 St Bernard Dr SE, Cullman, AL 35055

name: Vulcan Statue
remarks: A 56-foot iron statue of the Roman god Vulcan on a 124-foot pedestal overlooking Birmingham — the world's largest cast iron statue.

name: Unclaimed Baggage Center
remarks: The only store in the US selling unclaimed airline luggage — 50,000 square feet of lost clothing, electronics, and oddities.

name: World's Largest Office Chair
remarks: A 33-foot steel office chair erected in 2009 outside a furniture company to claim the world record for largest office chair.

name: The Crossroads (Robert Johnson)
remarks: The legendary intersection where blues icon Robert Johnson is said to have sold his soul to the devil in exchange for his guitar mastery.

name: International Car Forest of the Last Church
remarks: Dozens of cars and trucks planted nose-first into the Nevada desert in the tradition of Cadillac Ranch.

name: Extraterrestrial Highway Sign
remarks: The official highway sign for Nevada SR-375, dubbed the Extraterrestrial Highway by the state legislature due to UFO reports near Area 51.

name: Roswell UFO Museum
remarks: A museum dedicated to the 1947 Roswell incident, featuring alien exhibits, crash site theories, and extraterrestrial memorabilia.

name: Meow Wolf House of Eternal Return
remarks: A mind-bending immersive art installation and entertainment complex with interconnected surrealist rooms to explore.

name: Pistachioland
remarks: A roadside pistachio farm and gift shop crowned by a 30-foot pistachio statue built in 2008 to honor the farm's founder.

name: Bishop Castle
remarks: A towering hand-built stone castle constructed single-handedly by Jim Bishop starting in 1969, entirely without permits.

name: Casa Bonita
remarks: A legendary Mexican restaurant with cliff divers, caves, and entertainment inside a pink castle, made famous by South Park.

name: Celestial Seasonings Tea Factory
remarks: Free tours of the famous herbal tea factory including a nose-clearing Peppermint Room and a look at their iconic box artwork.

name: Albert the Bull
remarks: A 45-foot, 45-ton concrete Hereford bull billed as the world's largest bull statue.

name: Grotto of the Redemption
remarks: The world's largest man-made grotto, built by Father Paul Dobberstein from millions of rocks, gems, and minerals over 42 years.
address: 300 N Broadway St, West Bend, IA 50597

name: Iowa 80 Trucking Museum
remarks: Located at the world's largest truck stop, this free museum displays vintage trucks and extensive trucking memorabilia.

name: Gateway Arch
remarks: The iconic 630-foot stainless steel arch on the Mississippi riverfront, the tallest monument in the Western Hemisphere.

name: World's 2nd Largest Rocking Chair
remarks: A 42-foot rocking chair towering over Route 66 in Fanning, built to claim the world record before being surpassed.

name: Uranus Sideshow Museum
remarks: A Route 66 stop with fudge, two-headed animal oddities, a magic shop, and a name engineered purely for pun value.

name: House on the Rock
remarks: A surreal complex built atop a 60-foot rock chimney, filled with massive collections of oddities, automated orchestras, and the world's largest indoor carousel.

name: Mars Cheese Castle
remarks: A beloved Wisconsin roadside institution shaped like a castle and stocked wall-to-wall with Wisconsin cheeses and local foods.

name: National Freshwater Fishing Hall of Fame (Giant Muskie)
remarks: A 143-foot fiberglass muskie — the world's largest fish statue and largest fiberglass sculpture — with an observation deck inside its mouth.
address: 10360 Hall of Fame Dr, Hayward, WI 54843

name: Dinosaur Gardens
remarks: Life-sized concrete dinosaur sculptures in a wooded setting along US-23, featuring over 20 prehistoric creatures since the 1930s.

name: Hell, Michigan
remarks: A small town famous entirely for its name, with punny shops, a dam, and a tourism industry built around visiting Hell.

name: Longaberger Basket Building
remarks: A seven-story office building shaped exactly like a giant Longaberger picnic basket, complete with handles, built in 1997.

name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
remarks: An iconic I.M. Pei-designed glass pyramid on Lake Erie honoring the history of rock and roll music.

name: Hartman Rock Garden
remarks: A meticulously detailed miniature village of concrete sculptures built by Depression-era worker Ben Hartman starting in 1932.

name: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood Statue
remarks: A bronze statue of Fred Rogers on the North Shore waterfront commemorating the beloved TV host's Pittsburgh connection.
address: North Shore Dr & Federal St, Pittsburgh, PA 15212

name: Intercourse, Pennsylvania
remarks: An Amish village in Lancaster County famous for its name and as a gateway to Pennsylvania Dutch country, with dozens of craft shops.

name: Roadside America Miniature Village
remarks: An enormous indoor miniature village built over 60 years by Laurence Gieringer, featuring hundreds of hand-crafted scenes of American life.

name: World's Largest Kaleidoscope
remarks: A converted grain silo housing a 60-foot kaleidoscope with psychedelic 8-minute light shows, the largest kaleidoscope in the world.
address: 6 Rock City Rd, Mount Tremper, NY 12457

name: Boldt Castle
remarks: A 6-story, 120-room castle on Heart Island in the Thousand Islands, begun in 1900 as a gift of love and left unfinished after a tragedy.

name: Howe Caverns
remarks: A dramatic commercial cave attraction open since 1843, featuring an underground boat ride on a subterranean lake.

name: Coral Castle
remarks: A mysterious structure of massive coral rock sculptures built entirely in secret by one man, Ed Leedskalnin, over 28 years.

name: Solomon's Castle
remarks: A castle constructed from recycled newspaper printing plates by sculptor Howard Solomon, deep in the Florida swamplands.

name: Gatorland
remarks: An Old Florida classic open since 1949 with alligator and crocodile encounters, live shows, and a gaping gator-jaw entrance gate.
address: 14501 S Orange Blossom Trail, Orlando, FL 32837

name: Southernmost Point Buoy
remarks: A colorful concrete buoy marking the southernmost point in the continental US, one of the most photographed roadside spots in the country.
address: Whitehead St & South St, Key West, FL 33040

name: Weeki Wachee Springs (Live Mermaids)
remarks: A roadside theater since 1947 where live performers in mermaid costumes put on underwater shows in a natural freshwater spring.

name: Graceland
remarks: Elvis Presley's iconic home, now a museum and global pilgrimage site attracting over 600,000 fans annually.

name: Sunsphere
remarks: A 266-foot golden sphere-topped tower built for the 1982 World's Fair, offering 360-degree views of Knoxville and the Smokies.

name: Biltmore Estate
remarks: America's largest privately-owned home at 178,926 square feet, a Gilded Age chateau built by George Vanderbilt in 1895.

name: Vollis Simpson Whirligig Park
remarks: A park of massive hand-built wind-powered whirligig machines by folk artist Vollis Simpson, now a beloved public art landmark.

name: South of the Border
remarks: A kitschy roadside complex of motels, restaurants, and attractions straddling the NC-SC border, famous for its mile-long billboard campaign.

name: Peachoid Water Tower
remarks: A million-gallon water tower shaped and painted to look exactly like a giant peach, visible for miles along I-85.

name: Luray Caverns
remarks: The largest caverns in the eastern US, featuring the Great Stalacpipe Organ — the world's largest natural musical instrument.

name: Foamhenge
remarks: A full-scale Stonehenge replica made entirely of Styrofoam by artist Mark Cline, periodically relocated to new spots around Virginia.

name: World's Largest Penguin
remarks: A 27-foot concrete penguin welcoming travelers to Cut Bank, which bills itself as the coldest spot in the lower 48.
address: 1 S Central Ave, Cut Bank, MT 59427

name: Potato Museum
remarks: A quirky free museum celebrating Idaho's most famous crop, including the world's largest potato chip and dehydrated potato exhibits.

name: Hole N' the Rock
remarks: A 5,000-square-foot home carved entirely out of a sandstone rock face by Albert and Gladys Christensen over 12 years.

name: Gilgal Sculpture Garden
remarks: A hidden public garden with 12 original sculptures including a Sphinx bearing the face of Joseph Smith, built by Thomas Child.
address: 749 E 500 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84102

name: Painted Church
remarks: A small wooden church in Kona whose interior is painted with colorful biblical scenes created to teach scripture to early Hawaiian converts.
address: 84-5140 Painted Church Rd, Captain Cook, HI 96704

name: Igloo City (Abandoned Igloo Hotel)
remarks: An abandoned four-story hotel shaped like a giant igloo built in the 1970s along the Parks Highway, never completed due to code issues.

name: Jungle Gardens
remarks: A 170-acre botanical garden and bird sanctuary on the private island home of the McIlhenny Company, makers of Tabasco sauce.

name: Abita Mystery House (UCM Museum)
remarks: A folk art museum crammed with bizarre dioramas, the UnUsual Collection of Marvels, and a giant mechanical alligator named Darrell.

name: Crater of Diamonds
remarks: The world's only diamond-producing site open to the public where visitors dig and keep any gems they find — a real working diamond mine.

name: World's Largest Ball of Paint
remarks: A baseball that has had over 25,000 layers of paint applied by visitors since 1977, now weighing over 4,000 pounds.

name: Wigwam Village Inn No. 2
remarks: A 1937 motel with 15 concrete teepee-shaped rooms, one of only three surviving Wigwam Village motels left in the US.
address: 601 N Dixie Hwy, Cave City, KY 42127

name: World's Tallest Three-Story Building
remarks: The Shinner Building, recognized by Ripley's Believe It or Not as the world's tallest three-story building due to its unusually high ceilings.

name: L.L. Bean Flagship Store
remarks: The original L.L. Bean store, open 24 hours a day 365 days a year since 1951, with a giant boot sculpture at the entrance.

name: Paul Bunyan Statue
remarks: A 31-foot fiberglass statue of Paul Bunyan in his supposed birthplace, erected in 1959 to celebrate the city's centennial.

name: America's Stonehenge
remarks: A 4,000-year-old stone complex of chambers and astronomical alignments, sometimes called Mystery Hill, possibly pre-Columbian in origin.

name: Gillette Castle
remarks: A 24-room medieval-style stone castle built by eccentric actor William Gillette of Sherlock Holmes fame between 1914 and 1919.

name: WaterFire Providence
remarks: An award-winning public art installation of over 80 bonfires lit on the rivers of downtown Providence with live music accompaniment.

name: Hood Milk Bottle
remarks: A 40-foot milk bottle-shaped snack stand outside the Boston Children's Museum on Fort Point Channel, a landmark since 1977.

name: Lucy the Elephant
remarks: A six-story National Historic Landmark elephant structure built in 1881 as a real estate gimmick, once used as a tavern and hotel.

name: World's Largest Lightbulb
remarks: A giant lightbulb sculpture in the town where Thomas Edison invented the incandescent bulb, honoring his enduring legacy.

name: Grounds for Sculpture
remarks: A 42-acre sculpture park with over 270 works of contemporary art set among trees, ponds, and gardens on a former state fairgrounds.

name: Dogfish Head Brewery
remarks: The flagship brewery of the famous Dogfish Head craft beer brand, with tours, tasting rooms, and creative seasonal beers.

name: World's Largest Buffalo Monument
remarks: A 26-foot, 60-ton concrete bison sculpture towering over the North Dakota plains, completed in 1959.

name: Enchanted Highway
remarks: A 32-mile stretch of highway lined with massive scrap-metal sculptures by Gary Greff, including the world's largest scrap metal sculpture Geese in Flight.

name: Fargo Woodchipper Display
remarks: The actual woodchipper prop from the Coen Brothers' film Fargo, on display at the Visitor Center alongside a celebrity handprint walk.

name: Jackalope Square
remarks: A giant statue of the mythical jackalope in the town that claims to be its birthplace and sells official jackalope hunting licenses.

name: Mystery Hole
remarks: A classic gravity-defying mystery spot attraction on Route 60 near the New River Gorge area.

name: World's Largest Teapot
remarks: A 14-foot-tall and 14-foot-wide teapot-shaped roadside attraction originally built in 1938 as a root beer stand in the pottery capital of the US.

name: Bread and Puppet Theater Museum
remarks: A free museum in a converted barn displaying enormous papier-mache puppets used in decades of political street theater performances.

name: National Aquarium
remarks: One of the most visited aquariums in the US at Baltimore's Inner Harbor, housing over 20,000 animals across multiple ecosystems.

name: National Building Museum Great Hall
remarks: A massive Victorian-era building whose 75-foot Great Hall has hosted presidential inaugural balls — a jaw-dropping architectural detour in DC.
